label: Q02
question: Should the CalCOFI DB ingest only CalCOFI-program tows or the full global SIO PIC holdings?
context: The collection spans the globe (lat -69 to 85; lon -184 to 180; 1262 expeditions) including non-CalCOFI programs. SWFOrder_Occ is 99% null (only CalCOFI cruises populated); STATION_LINE/NUMBER are CalCOFI line/station for CalCOFI but Haul/Cycle for other programs.
answer: Decided CalCOFI-side (2026-08-05): ingest CalCOFI-program tows only, scoped by Expedition_Type_pnt == 'CalCOFI' (82,343 of 148,129 source rows). That flag is reliable - it agrees with 'CALCOFI' appearing in EXPEDITION_pnt on all 148,129 rows, with zero disagreement either way. This REPLACES the previous CalCOFI-region bounding-box proxy, which was wrong in both directions: it admitted 32,719 non-CalCOFI tows (CWPA Squid Survey, RACER, SOSO, HUNTINGTON BEACH, CCE-LTER ...) and excluded 15,532 genuine CalCOFI tows outside the modern grid - the 1950s-80s inshore, Gulf of California and Baja lines down to 19.9N. Those excluded tows are not coordinate errors (zero impossible coordinates) and resolve to a CalCOFI cruise 83.2% of the time, above the dataset average. Net effect on cruise_key coverage: 66.6% -> 82.1%.
who: Rasmus Swalethorp; Ed Weber; Linsey Sala

label: Q07
question: Does the PIC database hold a cod-end / net-side identifier (e.g. port vs starboard, net 1 vs net 2) that is not in this export - and can the ethanol-vs-formalin designation be used as a crosswalk to match a PIC net tow to the specific swfsc_ichthyo net from the same deployment?
context: A CalCOFI bongo (CB) deployment fishes paired cod ends: conventionally one is fixed in formalin and sorted for ichthyoplankton by SWFSC, the other goes to the SIO PIC. The two archives therefore describe the same physical tow from opposite cod ends, but neither export carries an identifier for WHICH cod end. In the CalCOFI subset PIC records 74,804 formaldehyde vs 7,538 ethanol/alcohol tows; swfsc_ichthyo holds 75,434 net records, 74,356 tows with a single net and only 1,078 with two. Without a cod-end key we can only join at tow grain (site + date), not net grain - so a PIC sample cannot be tied to the net whose volume_sampled / standard_haul_factor would normalize it to a density. A cod-end field, or a confirmed preservative->cod-end rule, would make the join exact.
answer: Linsey Sala's Parent Net Event (PNE) table (2026-10-19) gives each PIC record's preservative, which maps to the net side (formaldehyde = starboard, ethanol = port). CalCOFI/workflows#198 (libs/pic_net_match.R, explore_sio_pic-zooplankton_ichthyo-nets.qmd) matches 61,789 of 83,157 PIC records to SWFSC ichthyoplankton nets in release v2026.10.20 on station, time, net type (mapped to SWFSC tow type) and preservative (side), and records Ed's NetId as net_uuid; crosswalk delivered to Linsey 2026-10-21.
who: Ed Weber; Rasmus Swalethorp; Linsey Sala

label: Q10
question: Three cruises' net samples carry a ship that SWFSC's ichthyo database records for another vessel at the same station and time. Which ship took them: (a) 204 samples of 6401 (50 station occupations) named BLACK DOUGLAS (31BD), dated 1964-01-31 to 02-16, each within a median 6 h of an AGASSIZ (31AX) occupation of its station, at stations Black Douglas has no ichthyo tow at on that cruise; (b) 79 samples of 9608 (79 occupations) named NEW HORIZON (32NM), 1996-08-04 to 08-17, each within ~8 h of a MAKO (32QM) occupation; (c) 24 samples of 8407 (24 occupations) named DAVID STARR JORDAN (31JD), 1984-07-09 to 07-12, each within ~6 h of a NEW HORIZON (32NM) occupation?
context: In v2026.10.30 these samples key to the ship the PIC tow table names, so they join a cruise that has no ichthyo tow at their station that day. Your Parent Net Event crosswalk (v2026.10.20), which matches on station and date without the ship, agrees: 128 of 6401's nets matched SWFSC nets on 1964-01-31AX, and the 79 tows of 9608 found no New Horizon candidate. Two ships often worked one survey (6401 had Agassiz and Black Douglas; 9608 New Horizon and Mako), so a tow logged under the survey's lead ship would look exactly like this. Other pairs found by the same check are 1 to 2 samples each (two ships trading stations) and are not asked about. Found 2026-10-31 by the co-occupation check that followed the July 2009 McArthur fix (bottle Q19): a sample at a station SWFSC's ichthyo database occupied within 24 h under another cruise, and never under its own. check_cruise_key_integrity() check 11 only gates derived cruises, so a SWFSC-keyed pair like these is reported, not stopped. List by station and time: cruise_ship_pairs_by_station_v2026.10.30.csv (sent with the question).
proposed_answer: The ship that occupied the station is the one SWFSC records: the 6401 samples above were taken on the Agassiz, the 9608 samples on the Mako and the 8407 samples on the New Horizon. We would correct the ship for exactly these samples in metadata/cruise_ship_corrections.csv (keyed by cruise, station and date, not the whole cruise) until the PIC database is corrected, and say so in the release notes.
